difficultyRecalibration.description: Recalibrate ~50-60% of items downward by 1 tier per DL-031. Must happen DURING certification waves, not post-hoc per D-Program C2 lesson.

exhibitVerification.description: Verify ~24 exhibits across 15 cases. Check: internal consistency, every row consumed by ≥1 item, subtotals sum correctly. D-Program had 0 exhibits — this is entirely new work.

top10.issue: Shortest explanation in entire pool (21 chars). Zero educational content. F-domain topic requires unfamiliar data governance frameworks.
top10.mitigation: Must be completely rewritten as a mini-lesson with DAMA-DMBOK citation, data quality dimensions, and warranty analytics context.

top10.issue: Second-shortest explanation (24 chars). Prompt wording ambiguous: 'current-month cash collections from current-month sales' could confuse with total collections.
top10.mitigation: Clarify prompt. Rewrite explanation with collection-timing breakdown, cash-vs-accrual trap warning.

top10.issue: Both test the same quality-cost classification concept. Redundant pair — no additional pedagogical value. Agent C flags RED-001.
top10.mitigation: Replace one item (preferably Q6, the match-type at 58 chars) with a new concept: process improvement metrics or cost of quality trend analysis.

top10.issue: Ambiguous prompt wording: 'before income-tax cash effects not listed' may confuse candidates. Explanation only 54 chars.
top10.mitigation: Rewrite prompt to clarify operating vs. financing classification. Expand explanation with ASC 230 walk-through.

top10.issue: CalculationRequired: true on multi type (schema error). Generic 92-char explanation with no distractor rationale at Evaluate level.
top10.mitigation: Fix schema error. Add per-choice distractor rationale inline in Explanation.

top10.issue: ~50-60% of items labeled Moderate/3 or Difficult/4 that should be 1-2 tiers lower. Simple arithmetic items labeled Moderate; definition-match items labeled Difficult.
top10.mitigation: Recalibrate DURING each wave (not post-hoc per D-Program C2 lesson). Apply recalibration BEFORE certifying items.

top10.issue: Avg 80 chars vs. D-Program post-cert 1,282 chars. 0% distractor coverage, 1% exam traps, 11% business interpretation. 17 DEFECTIVE items below EV1 threshold (50 chars).
top10.mitigation: Enforce 500-char minimum quality floor across ALL waves (Agent I Blindspot #4). Use D-Program explanation templates.

top10.issue: Cross-domain E,F cases in the final wave. COSO + NIST + COBIT dual citations required. Team fatigue at end of program. SOX 404 + ITGC + RPA governance + cybersecurity — most complex topic cluster.
top10.mitigation: Schedule as 3 sequential sub-sessions within Wave 6 (E1 → quality gate → E2 → quality gate → F2). Do not attempt all 3 in one pass.

top10.issue: Select/multi/match items where no calculation is needed have CalculationRequired: true. Metadata accuracy defect across Waves 1-6.
top10.mitigation: Batch-fix at Wave 0 or Wave 1. Correct each before certifying the parent item.

top10.issue: scored_cases.js contains both CBQ-* cases (90 items) AND 15 legacy cases (CASE-A1, CASE-B1, etc., ~120 items). Write operations must ONLY touch CBQ-* items. Cross-contamination risk per Agent I Challenge #7.
top10.mitigation: Validate before every write: grep for modified CASE-* ItemIDs. Add pre-write/post-write diff check to wave protocol.

5_COMPARISON_TO_D_PROGRAM.summaryVerdict: ENHANCED_CASE_BASE is 1.4× more complex and requires ~4× more agent-hours than D-Program, but is LOWER architectural risk due to single-block structure and no DL-008/DL-016 vulnerability.

dimensionComparison.effortImpact: Front-loaded quality assurance (BETTER outcome, more effort)
Fewer structural defect categories to fix (BETTER)

whyEffortIsHigher: PRIMARY DRIVER — Explanation gap: BASE avg 80 chars vs D-Program pre-cert ~120 chars. BASE needs 10× expansion vs D-Program's 8×. This alone adds ~30% to explanation authoring effort.

SECONDARY — Exhibits: D-Program had 0 exhibits to verify. BASE has ~24 exhibits requiring data-consistency checks, row-consumption validation, and subtotal reconciliation. This is ~2h of entirely new work.

TERTIARY — Wave 0: D-Program did not have a formal pre-certification audit. BASE injects 13h of audit work before any certification writes occur. This is a quality improvement over D-Program but adds to total effort.
MODERATING FACTOR — Experience: Team has D-Program's playbook, templates, and lessons learned. Agent efficiency should be 20-30% higher than during first-time D-Program certification.

MODERATING FACTOR — Lower quality target: BASE targets 800+ avg vs D-Program's 1,282. This is a conscious trade-off: the last remaining Unprocessed array can accept a slightly lower ceiling since 7 of 9 arrays are already Certified.

processGaps.gap: No automated exhibit data verification tool

processGaps.description: Agents have less experience with F-domain (data governance, analytics, RPA, cybersecurity) vs. A-E domains. This showed in D-Program's lower explanation quality on D6/D12.

processGaps.gap: No ExplanationWrong fields in case-study architecture

processGaps.description: D-Program had 2 backup violations (S525/S526 .bak files in root). With 6 waves, the risk of backup-path errors accumulates.
processGaps.mitigation: Governance agent must verify backup placement BEFORE and AFTER each wave write. Add to pre-flight checklist.

processGaps.description: The same file (scored_cases.js) contains both CBQ-* cases (90 items) and legacy CASE-* cases (~120 items). Write operations must ONLY modify CBQ-* item blocks.
